ap_psychology-m01.set_intro: A clinician records the following information during an intake visit with a 34-year-old adult who sought help because of constant worry.

rows: Worries about money, health, and work almost every day
Repeated unwanted thoughts that are neutralized by rituals

items.stem: Which diagnostic category best fits the information in the intake record?

options.text: Specific phobia, because the worry is linked to health and work
options.why: The record shows no avoidance of specific places or objects, and the worry covers many topics.

options.text: Generalized anxiety disorder, because the worry is excessive, long-lasting, and accompanied by tension and sleep problems
options.why: Persistent worry about many topics with physical symptoms and no panic attacks or rituals points to generalized anxiety.

options.text: Obsessive-compulsive disorder, because the person experiences repeated worry
options.why: The record shows no rituals performed to neutralize unwanted thoughts.

options.text: Panic disorder, because the person experiences frequent physical symptoms
options.why: The record shows no sudden episodes of intense fear, which panic disorder requires.

items.stem: A cognitive therapist works with this person. Which action is the therapist most likely to take?

options.text: Reward the person with praise each time a calm behavior is shown
options.why: Reinforcing target behaviors is a behavioral technique, not the cognitive approach.

options.text: Help the person identify catastrophic predictions and test them against evidence
options.why: Cognitive therapy changes the thought patterns that maintain anxiety.

options.text: Repeatedly accept the person's feelings without offering any interpretation
options.why: Unconditional acceptance without interpretation is characteristic of the humanistic approach.

options.text: Ask the person to describe early childhood memories to uncover hidden conflicts
options.why: Exploring unconscious conflicts from childhood is a psychodynamic approach.

items.stem: Which detail in the record is most useful for ruling out panic disorder?

options.why: Age alone does not distinguish panic disorder from other anxiety disorders.

options.text: The complaint has lasted more than 8 months
options.why: A long duration is consistent with several anxiety disorders and does not separate panic disorder from the others.

options.text: No sudden episodes of intense fear are reported
options.why: Panic disorder is defined by recurrent sudden episodes of intense fear.

options.text: The person reports muscle tension and restlessness
options.why: These symptoms occur in several anxiety disorders and do not rule out panic disorder.
